paper.title: Kullback-Leibler Maillard Sampling for Multi-armed Bandits with Bounded Rewards

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with reward distributions supported on [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: In this paper, we study the multi-armed bandit setting where reward distributions of all arms are supported on $[0,1]$. ... The goal of the agent is to minimize its pseudo-regret over $T$ time steps: $\Reg(T) = T \mu^* - \EE\sum_{t=1}^T y_t$

bound.expression: T*Delta_thr + sum_subopt(Delta_i*log(Max(T*kl(mu_i + c*Delta_i, mu_star - c*Delta_i), exp(2)))/kl(mu_i + c*Delta_i, mu_star - c*Delta_i)) + 392*sum_subopt(((mu_star*(1-mu_star) + Delta_i)/(c**2*Delta_i))*log(Max(Min((mu_star*(1-mu_star) + Delta_i)/(c**2*Delta_i**2), c**2*T*Delta_i**2/(mu_star*(1-mu_star) + Delta_i)), exp(2))))
bound.expression_latex: T\Delta + \sum_{a: \Delta_a > \Delta} \frac{\Delta_a \ln(T \kl(\mu_a + c \Delta_a, \mu_1 - c \Delta_a) \vee e^2 )}{\kl(\mu_a + c \Delta_a, \mu_1 - c \Delta_a)} + 392 \sum_{a: \Delta_a > \Delta} \rbr{\frac{\dmu_1 + \Delta_a}{c^2 \Delta_a}} \ln\rbr{ \rbr{ \frac{\dmu_1 + \Delta_a}{c^2 \Delta_a^2} \wedge \frac{c^2 T \Delta_a^2}{\dmu_1 + \Delta_a }} \vee e^2 }
bound.regime: any Delta_thr >= 0, c in (0, 1/4]; sums restricted to arms with Delta_i > Delta_thr

source.label: thm:expected-regret-total
source.quote: For any $K$-arm bandit problem with reward distribution supported on $[0,1]$, KL-MS has regret bounded as follows. For any $\Delta \geq 0$ and $c \in (0, \frac14]$: \Reg(T) \leq T\Delta + \sum_{a: \Delta_a > \Delta} \frac{\Delta_a \ln(T \kl(\mu_a + c \Delta_a, \mu_1 - c \Delta_a) \vee e^2 )}{\kl(\mu_a + c \Delta_a, \mu_1 - c \Delta_a)} + 392 \sum_{a: \Delta_a > \Delta} ...

results.notes: sum_subopt here is over arms with Delta_i > Delta_thr, not all suboptimal arms. mu_1 = mu_star (arms sorted). Note proof's constant derivation is somewhat inconsistent (c^2 vs c^4) but recorded as stated.

bound.regime: any Delta_thr >= 0; sum over arms with Delta_i > Delta_thr

source.label: lem:kl-ms-pre-sub-ucb
source.quote: For KL-MS, its regret is bounded by: for any $\Delta \geq 0$, \Reg(T) \leq T\Delta + O\del{\sum_{a: \Delta_a > \Delta} \rbr{\frac{\dmu_1 + \Delta_a}{\Delta_a}} \ln\rbr{ \frac{T\Delta_a^2}{\dmu_1 + \Delta_a} \vee e^2 }}

results.notes: T*Delta_thr term is exact, the rest is O(.).

source.label: thm:sub-UCB
source.quote: KL-MS's regret is bounded by $\Reg(T) \lesssim \sum_{a: \Delta_a > 0} \frac{\ln T}{\Delta_a}$. Therefore, KL-MS is sub-UCB.

source.label: thm:minimax-regret-bound
source.quote: For any $K$-arm bandit problem with reward distribution supported on $[0,1]$, KL-MS has regret bounded as: $\Reg(T) \lesssim \sqrt{\dmu_1 KT\ln{K}} + K \ln T$.

source.label: thm:asymptotic-optimality
source.quote: For any $K$-arm bandit problem with reward distribution supported on $[0,1]$, KL-MS satisfies the following asymptotic regret upper bound: \limsup_{T \rightarrow \infty} \fr{ \Reg(T) }{\ln(T)} = \sum_{a\in[K]:\Delta_a>0} \frac{\Delta_a}{\kl(\mu_a, \mu_1)}

results.notes: Stated with '=' but proven as '<='. Asymptotically optimal for Bernoulli rewards.

bound.expression: T*Delta_thr + sum_subopt(Delta_i*log(1 + T*log(T)**2)/kl(mu_i + c*Delta_i, mu_star - c*Delta_i)) + O(sum_subopt((mu_star*(1-mu_star) + Delta_i)/(c**2*Delta_i)))
bound.regime: any Delta_thr > 0, c in (0,1/4]; sums over arms with Delta_i > Delta_thr

source.label: thm:kl-ucb-refined
source.quote: For any $K$-arm bandit problem with reward distributions supported on $[0,1]$, KL-UCB (Algorithm~\ref{alg:kl-ucb}) has regret bounded as follows. For any $\Delta > 0$ and $c \in (0,\frac14]$, ...

results.notes: Refined analysis (proof sketch) of existing algorithm; mixed exact/O expression.

bound.expression_latex: O\rbr{ \sqrt{ \dmu_1 T K \ln T } + K \ln T}

source.label: thm:kl-ucb-refined
source.quote: and consequently, \Reg(T) \leq O\rbr{ \sqrt{ \dmu_1 T K \ln T } + K \ln T}.

bound.expression_latex: O\rbr{ \sqrt{ \dmu_1 T K^3 \ln T } + K^2 \ln T}

source.label: thm:kl-ucb++-refined
source.quote: For any $K$-arm bandit problem with reward distributions supported on $[0,1]$, KL-UCB++ \Reg(T) \leq O\rbr{ \sqrt{ \dmu_1 T K^3 \ln T } + K^2 \ln T}.

results.notes: KL-UCB++ uses T and K in its index.

source.label: thm:ucb-v-refined
source.quote: The regret of the algorithm UCB-V\cite{audibert09exploration} is bounded by: \Reg(T) \lsim \sqrt{\dmu_1 K T \ln(T)} + K\ln(T)

results.notes: Horizon knowledge of UCB-V version not specified in this paper.
